facts.text: Residual safe distance is the gap deliberately left between a stopped machine and an object so that the stop is a near miss rather than contact.
facts.quote: Residual safe distance is the gap deliberately left between the stopped machine and the object, so that a stop is a near miss and not a light touch.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 defines safe distance as a safe offset set by an authorized person plus measurement error.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 defines a "safe distance" as a safe offset set by an authorized person plus the measurement error

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 makes safe distance the final term in the collision-system distance, after detection, determination, action and machine stopping.
facts.quote: makes it the final term in the collision-system distance after detection, determination, action and machine stopping [Chapter 3]

facts.text: The booklet's trigger-distance formulas represent residual safe distance as D_safe or D_safety, the last item in the trigger distance.
facts.quote: In the booklet's formulas it appears as D_safe or D_safety, the last item in the trigger distance [Chapter 8].

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 leaves the value of safe distance to the site.
facts.quote: The standard leaves the value to the site.

facts.text: The South African MOSH specification uses stop gaps of 1.0 to 4.0 m at speeds of 10 km/h or less.
facts.quote: The South African MOSH specification uses stop gaps of 1.0 to 4.0 m at 10 km/h or less

facts.text: The South African MOSH specification uses stop gaps of 15 m plus or minus 5 m at speeds above 10 km/h.
facts.quote: 15 m plus or minus 5 m above 10 km/h

facts.text: The South African MOSH specification specifies position accuracy of 1.5 m or 10 percent.
facts.quote: with a position accuracy of 1.5 m or 10 percent [Chapter 3]

facts.text: Field measurements found that installed stop zones varied between sites by up to 3.6 m.
facts.quote: installed stop zones varied between sites by up to 3.6 m

facts.text: Repeat field measurements of stop zones at one site agreed within about 13 cm.
facts.quote: repeat measurements at one site agreed within about 13 cm [Chapter 8]

facts.text: Residual safe distance must absorb sensor position error, uncertainty in predicted stopping distance, and small movements of the object.
facts.quote: The residual distance must absorb sensor position error, the uncertainty in the predicted stopping distance, and small movements of the object.

facts.text: The booklet's acceptance list calls for every test to report minimum stopping margin and residual impact speed.
facts.quote: The booklet's acceptance list includes "minimum stopping margin" and "residual impact speed" as quantities every test should report [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Simulation model-form, numerical and input uncertainty must be demonstrably smaller than the residual safe-distance margin: if the risk area leaves X meters of margin, those uncertainties must be smaller than X.
facts.quote: if the risk area leaves X meters of margin, the model-form, numerical and input uncertainty must be demonstrably smaller than X [Chapter 10]

facts.text: A larger residual safe-distance margin protects against error but causes more nuisance stops in close-proximity work, making the margin a tuning decision rather than a fixed constant.
facts.quote: A larger margin protects against error but brings more nuisance stops in close-proximity work, so it is a tuning decision, not a fixed constant.
